scope: Official Messages streaming protocol and official Python SDK compared with current shared parser, HTTP and capture source. This is research, not a review receipt or closure claim.

documented_facts.fact: Messages flow starts with message_start, contains indexed content blocks, then one or more message_delta events and a final message_stop. A block can have no delta events.
message_delta usage counts are cumulative; ping may occur any number of times; an SSE error is an API error; consumers should handle newly added event types gracefully.

The SDK initializes its snapshot from message_start. Later message_delta replaces output_tokens and replaces optional input/cache counters only when non-null. MessageDeltaUsage requires integer output_tokens; input/cache counters default to None. Thus missing optional counters retain prior values. Missing output_tokens acceptance is a compatible-provider extension, not official schema behavior.

The SDK yields message_stop without breaking its transport loop, ignores ping, and filters unrecognized top-level event names. These branches are independent of prior message_stop. An error raises immediately. JSON decoding is attempted for error bodies; malformed text and empty text also reach status-error construction. The transport is closed in finally.

get_final_message consumes the iterator to completion. The SDK does not explicitly convert a timeout or cancellation after message_stop into successful get_final_message return. Its message_stop helper attaches the accumulated Message; get_final_text separately requires text content.

stop_reason is null at message_start and supplied in message_delta. end_turn can legitimately accompany empty content. max_tokens is a successful response stop reason indicating truncation, including potentially incomplete tool input. tool_use ends the current response while requesting tool execution; it need not contain visible prose. Therefore protocol termination is not proof of a finished novel artifact.
An API version can gain output values and new enum-like variants, explicitly including stream event types. Version 2023-06-01 uses named events and removed the unnecessary [DONE] marker.

Status-error construction accepts body as object and selects exception class by HTTP status. For HTTP 200 carrying an SSE error it falls through to APIStatusError. It does not assume body.error is a mapping to select that exception.

recommended_local_rules.rule: Keep one protocol-owned cumulative snapshot. Replace each present validated counter; retain omitted optionals. Do not sum cumulative snapshots or select unrelated nested billing aliases. Only the final validated pre-terminal snapshot has canonical response usage authority. Preserve this repository's existing cache-inclusive input projection separately from raw input_tokens.

Preserving omitted output_tokens retains the current compatible-adapter behavior. Explicit null output_tokens remains typed invalid. Optional null input/cache counters retain prior values. Do not claim all these omission rules come from the official required-output schema.

Classify valid ping before, during and after message_stop as IGNORE_TRANSPORT_KEEPALIVE; never mutate Message, usage, content, or stop reason. Keep bounded counters as diagnostics. Do not reinterpret a known semantic event carrying ping-like fields as keepalive.

Separate semantic terminal proof, durable capture of that proof, and clean transport close. After a fully validated message_stop and durable terminal capture, timeout/cancellation preserves the first two and records an unclean tail. Before valid terminal proof these remain typed failures. This differs from SDK convenience-method transport exhaustion, and documentation does not directly specify it.

Once an ordered authoritative Provider error is observed, freeze semantic consumption immediately; retain later ping, EOF, timeout, cancellation and malformed tail only as diagnostics. First Provider error stays primary. Do not search across an earlier malformed/invalid prefix to grant a later error precedence.

message_stop followed by an explicit Provider error is Provider failure, not silent success. The SDK continues reading and raises this error. Successful terminal proof may be retained as historical evidence, but must not retain successful result authority.

A closed named error frame is safely normalized for object, unexpected object, string, number, boolean, array, null, raw malformed and empty payloads. Guard every mapping access. Record fixed safe message, payload shape/hash/byte length, allowlisted error type, and event ordinal. Raw Provider message text is not a safe public message. Raw event-name/type conflicts need their own diagnostic; never convert error into keepalive.

Recommended forward compatibility: consistently framed unknown top-level event names produce VERSIONED_UNKNOWN_EVENT_POLICY with diagnostic ignore and no semantic mutation. Unknown subtypes inside a known semantic event, name/type conflicts, non-object semantic payloads and unsupported semantic continuation remain typed fail-closed. Document this distinction explicitly; graceful handling is not permission to guess unknown content semantics.

EOF after valid message_stop succeeds; EOF beforehand is typed missing-terminal failure. Require the entire ordered prefix to validate, including block closure and stop reason. A lexical message_stop or [DONE] alone cannot prove Anthropic completion. Duplicate stop and known semantic events after stop fail with precise typed protocol causes.

Empty or reasoning-only end_turn, max_tokens and tool/schema responses can be protocol-terminal while still failing or requiring recovery at the existing business/artifact boundary. Do not demand visible prose in the transport parser, fabricate final text from reasoning, treat max_tokens as transport loss, or bypass tool/schema validation.

Register framing exits as well as decoded event classes: malformed JSON/UTF-8, missing frame delimiter, event/data conflict, absent/non-object semantic payload, SSE comments/ignored fields, and non-SSE JSON response fallback. Existing [DONE] support must be protocol-specific. Unknown event behavior must also agree with usage extraction and terminal-capture detection.

local_source_observations.observed: Current parser uses message_started/message_stopped/message_delta_seen/open_blocks. It handles error before ping before post-stop rejection, accumulates usage through the shared merge, and requires closed blocks plus stop reason at message_stop. Unknown events fail. Known text/tool/thinking/redacted_thinking blocks form its current finite block subset.
Ordered adapter validation grants Provider-error authority; other parser exceptions return None. This helper alone cannot expose every precise protocol failure to interrupted HTTP handling.

HTTP gathers bytes before parse. Interrupted reads inspect Provider error, detect terminal bytes, capture with transport_complete=false, then recover terminal timeout/cancel. Semantic recovery already exists, but capture transport metadata is separate and must not downgrade durable terminal proof.

Closed-frame decoder normalizes named error even when JSON is malformed/non-object, keeps post-error diagnostics, validates name/type conflict, and rejects unterminated data frames. It does not validate the semantic prefix itself.

Cross-protocol terminal hint uses decoded final event or message_stop followed by pings. It is intentionally only a byte hint, cannot prove semantic validity, and its generic parsing can disagree with Anthropic error normalization/unknown-tail policy.

Usage merge retains omitted fields and non-output nulls, validates nonnegative integer counters, and sums distinct final input/cache fields. Extraction independently owns a message_stopped check and ignores ping; this is a sibling protocol decision surface that must agree with the shared state machine.

Existing normalization guards mapping accesses, separates boolean from number, fixes public safe_message, hashes raw data, allowlists Provider error types, and stores bounded secondary-tail evidence. It is suitable to preserve, not reconstruct.

research_limits: Official sources were browsed; no credentials or Provider endpoints were accessed. A direct shell attempt to retrieve public official GitHub sources was denied by network sandbox and produced no downloaded evidence.

SDK URLs are moving main references observed on the stated date. An immutable commit lookup and retrieval of the prior locally cited 62de60b27d04f0927a0ccf0f2610597fafcfab6a revision were unavailable. No immutable source hash is claimed.
Official docs do not explicitly specify post-message_stop timeout/cancellation result preservation or privacy-safe tail capture; these recommendations are local policy bound to the Master.

This report does not assert generated matrix coverage, regression status, request equivalence, historical replay pass, independent review pass, or execution eligibility. Those require separate mechanical evidence.
